research_mode: official UK government and ONS primary statistical releases and methodology only; every claim carries a fail-closed limitation; no parcel result, exact incident location, candidate value, local risk score or business result claimed

sources.publisher: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology and Home Office
sources.name: Cyber survey commissioners
verified_claims: The 2025/2026 survey was commissioned by DSIT and the Home Office.
limitations: Commissioning does not make self-reported incidents complete administrative records.

sources.publisher: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology and Home Office
sources.name: Cyber survey organisational scope
verified_claims: The main report covers UK businesses and charities, with education results in a separate annex.
limitations: Main-report percentages must not be applied to public-sector education institutions.

sources.publisher: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology and Home Office
sources.name: Cyber survey fieldwork
verified_claims: Quantitative and qualitative fieldwork took place between August and December 2025.
limitations: The estimates describe a survey period rather than continuous monitoring.

sources.publisher: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology and Home Office
sources.name: Identified-breach limitation
verified_claims: The survey includes only attacks organisations identified and were willing to report.
limitations: The reported prevalence likely understates hidden or unidentified attacks.

sources.publisher: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology and Home Office
sources.name: Business cyber-breach prevalence
verified_claims: Forty-three percent of businesses reported a breach or attack in the previous 12 months.
limitations: A survey percentage is not evidence that a specific business was attacked.

sources.publisher: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology and Home Office
sources.name: Charity cyber-breach prevalence
verified_claims: Twenty-eight percent of charities reported a breach or attack in the previous 12 months.
limitations: Charity results must not be substituted for business or parcel risk.

sources.publisher: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology and Home Office
sources.name: Cyber population extrapolation
verified_claims: The survey extrapolated identified breaches to about 612,000 businesses and 57,000 charities.
limitations: Population estimates are subject to sampling error and identification bias.

sources.publisher: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology and Home Office
sources.name: Business-size cyber gradient
verified_claims: Reported prevalence was 42% for micro, 46% for small, 65% for medium and 69% for large businesses.
limitations: Size-group rates do not predict the status of an individual organisation.

sources.publisher: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology and Home Office
sources.name: Cyber crime subset rule
verified_claims: Cyber crimes are a subset of cyber breaches and attacks and are presented as distinct figures.
limitations: The two series must not be added as independent event totals.

sources.publisher: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology and Home Office
sources.name: Phishing prevalence
verified_claims: Phishing was reported by 38% of businesses and 25% of charities.
limitations: Reported phishing exposure may omit attacks not recognised by respondents.

sources.publisher: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology and Home Office
sources.name: Phishing-only share
verified_claims: Among breached organisations, phishing-only incidents rose to 51% for businesses and 57% for charities.
limitations: The share is conditional on organisations reporting a breach.

sources.publisher: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology and Home Office
sources.name: Ransomware prevalence
verified_claims: Reported ransomware among businesses was 1%, down from 3% in each of the previous two survey years.
limitations: Small percentage changes are subject to survey uncertainty.

sources.publisher: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology and Home Office
sources.name: Cyber survey sample
verified_claims: The quantitative survey included 2,112 businesses, 1,085 charities and 577 education institutions.
limitations: Subgroup estimates have wider margins of error than the full sample.

sources.publisher: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology and Home Office
sources.name: Cyber survey official-statistics status
verified_claims: The survey is labelled official statistics and produced under the Code of Practice for Statistics.
limitations: Official status does not remove sampling and response limitations.

sources.publisher: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology and Home Office
sources.name: Cyber incidence wording break
verified_claims: Overall incidence results are comparable only from 2023/2024 onward because the question wording changed.
limitations: Earlier years must not be placed in the same incidence trend without adjustment.

sources.publisher: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology and Home Office
sources.name: Weighted-estimate rule
verified_claims: Final estimates use weighted samples to represent the populations of businesses and charities with employees.
limitations: Weighting does not eliminate non-response or measurement error.

sources.publisher: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology and Home Office
sources.name: Business margin of error example
verified_claims: At an estimated 50% based on 2,112 businesses, the stated 95% margin of error is about plus or minus 2.6 percentage points.
limitations: The exact uncertainty differs by estimate and subgroup.

sources.publisher: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology and Home Office
sources.name: Formal incident-response planning
verified_claims: Only 25% of businesses reported having a formal incident-response plan.
limitations: Plan presence does not prove operational effectiveness.

sources.publisher: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology and Home Office
sources.name: Medium-business board updates
verified_claims: The share of medium businesses receiving at least annual cyber updates fell from 78% to 70%.
limitations: The survey does not establish why the change occurred.

sources.publisher: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology and Home Office
sources.name: Charity cyber priority
verified_claims: The share of charities treating cyber security as a high priority fell from 68% to 60%.
limitations: Stated priority is self-reported and not a direct control-maturity score.
